tasks.title: THE MISMATCH
tasks.prompt: What is established by the incident card and approved run sheet?

options.text: Team Comet voluntarily ended its demo early.
The judges changed the slot before the demo.
The demo played for 42 seconds even though the approved cue called for a 2-minute file.
Team Orbit’s video was played instead of Comet’s.

tasks.explanation: The demo ran 42 seconds although the approved cue called for 2:00.
reference_sql: select evidence_id, title from evidence_phase_1 where evidence_id in ('E01', 'E02') order by evidence_id

tasks.title: WHAT THE RECEIPT PROVES
tasks.prompt: What does Dev’s submission receipt rule out?

options.text: The final 2-minute file was successfully submitted before the cutoff.
Dev personally loaded the USB drive.
The playback machine used the submitted file.
No one could access the AV booth after submission.

tasks.explanation: The receipt proves a 2-minute file was submitted before the cutoff and nothing about playback.
reference_sql: select evidence_id, title from evidence_phase_1 where evidence_id in ('E03') order by evidence_id

tasks.title: THE SEALED DRIVE
tasks.prompt: What is the strongest conclusion from the handoff log and seal record?

options.text: Arjun edited the file after receiving the drive.
Tara must have changed the file because she wrote the labels.
The sealed drive contained the correct file beyond doubt.
Arjun’s logged custody does not explain the mismatch; the drive was returned with its seal intact.

tasks.explanation: The drive was returned with the seal intact, so Arjun's custody does not explain the mismatch.
reference_sql: select evidence_id, title from evidence_phase_2 where evidence_id in ('E05') order by evidence_id

tasks.title: THE EXPORT HISTORY
tasks.prompt: What does the export history establish when compared with the playback report?

options.text: Tara exported the file because she wrote the label.
A short rehearsal source was exported under Nisha’s account using the same filename as the final file.
The final file was corrupted during Dev’s upload.
The player automatically shortened any video to 42 seconds.

tasks.explanation: A 42-second file from the rehearsal source was exported under Nisha's account with the final filename.
reference_sql: select evidence_id, title from evidence_phase_2 where evidence_id in ('E06', 'E07') order by evidence_id

tasks.title: THE REFLECTION PHOTO
tasks.prompt: Why is the booth reflection photo important?

options.text: It independently places Nisha at the workstation during the short export, while still not proving intent on its own.
It proves Nisha wrote every line in the source video.
It proves Tara never entered the booth.
It proves the judges requested a shorter demo.

tasks.explanation: The photo independently places Nisha at the workstation during the export without proving intent.
reference_sql: select evidence_id, title from evidence_phase_2 where evidence_id in ('E07') order by evidence_id
select evidence_id, title from evidence_phase_3 where evidence_id in ('E09') order by evidence_id

tasks.title: THE BEST EXPLANATION
tasks.prompt: Which explanation best accounts for the complete evidence set?

options.text: Dev uploaded a corrupted final file, and the playback machine shortened it.
Arjun broke the seal and replaced the file after collection.
Nisha knowingly exported the 42-second rehearsal cut under the final filename before the drive was sealed, intending to disrupt Comet’s reveal and create an opening for Orbit.
Tara accidentally mislabeled a correct two-minute file, causing the player to stop early.

tasks.explanation: Only the explanation that fits the file trail, the timing before sealing, the photo and the cue draft.
reference_sql: select evidence_id, title from evidence_phase_2 where evidence_id in ('E07') order by evidence_id
select evidence_id, title from evidence_phase_3 where evidence_id in ('E09', 'E10', 'E11', 'E12') order by evidence_id
